question: What is the main job of anticoagulant drugs?

options.B: Prevent new blood clots from forming

explanation: Think of anticoagulants as a shield rather than a cleaner. They stop new clots from forming, but they don't dissolve the ones already there. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h1)

question: Why do patients on blood thinners still rely on their body's natural healing to clear old clots?

options.A: Natural defenses are permanently shut down by the drugs
options.B: Medications destroy platelets before they reach the clot
options.C: Anticoagulants lack the ability to break down established fibrin
options.D: Anticoagulants only slow down the heart rate

explanation: Anticoagulants prevent new trouble, but breaking down existing clots is a job for the body's own natural cleaning system! Great job reviewing this. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h1)

question: How does heparin mainly work in the body?

options.B: By binding directly to blood platelets

explanation: Heparin teams up with a helper in your blood called antithrombin III to quickly put the brakes on clotting factors. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h2)

question: Warfarin stops blood clotting by interfering with which substances in the liver?
explanation: Warfarin works right in the liver, blocking vitamin K so it can't help build those important clotting factors. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h2)

question: Which lab test is checked regularly for a patient on an unfractionated heparin drip?
explanation: We use the aPTT test to make sure our patient is getting just the right amount of heparin—not too little, not too much. Perfect clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h3)

question: A patient on heparin suddenly has a very low platelet count and a new leg clot. What is going on?
explanation: This tricky reaction is called Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT). It causes platelets to drop while paradoxically forming new clots. Excellent clinical awareness! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h3)

question: What is the target INR range for a standard patient taking warfarin for deep vein thrombosis?
explanation: An INR of 2.0 to 3.0 is the sweet spot for warfarin therapy—it keeps clots away without letting bleeding get out of hand. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h4)

question: Why must patients on warfarin keep their daily intake of green leafy vegetables steady?

options.A: High fiber diets speed up kidney excretion of the drug
options.B: Vitamins in plants cause rapid breakdown of red blood cells
options.C: Vegetables contain vitamin K which directly counteracts warfarin
options.D: Leafy greens bind to the stomach wall and block absorption

explanation: Green veggies are packed with vitamin K. Big changes in your diet can mess with your warfarin dose, so consistency is key! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h4)

question: What is a major perk of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared to warfarin?

options.A: They use fixed dosing without routine lab monitoring
options.B: They can be easily reversed with green leafy vegetables
options.C: They have no risk of bleeding complications
options.D: They require daily blood tests for safety

explanation: DOACs are super convenient because patients take a standard pill without needing constant needle pricks for lab tests. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h5)

question: Which organ function must a nurse check before a patient starts a direct oral anticoagulant?
explanation: Since these drugs leave the body through the kidneys, checking kidney function first keeps the patient safe from drug buildup. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h5)

question: Why do patients with atrial fibrillation need anticoagulant medications?

options.A: To normalize a rapid irregular heart rate
options.B: To prevent stroke caused by blood clots in the atria
options.C: To dissolve fatty plaque buildup in coronary arteries
options.D: To lower systemic high blood pressure levels

explanation: In atrial fibrillation, blood can pool in the heart and form clots that might travel to the brain. Thinners protect them from strokes! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h6)

question: A patient is back on the ward after a total hip replacement. What is the best step to prevent blood clots in the legs?

options.A: Apply tight compression wraps to both legs permanently
options.B: Administer high-dose vitamin K supplements immediately
options.C: Restrict the patient to complete bed rest for one week

explanation: Major bone surgery puts patients at high risk for clots, so preventive blood thinners are a standard lifesaver. Excellent nursing choice! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h6)

question: What medication is given immediately to reverse a heparin overdose?
explanation: Protamine sulfate is the fast-acting antidote that neutralizes heparin right away in an emergency. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h7)

question: Which sign strongly suggests internal bleeding in a patient on blood thinners?

options.A: Complaints of severe itching on the arms and legs
options.B: A sudden rise in the patient's body temperature
options.C: An increase in urine output over twenty-four hours
options.D: The presence of dark, tarry stools in the bedpan

explanation: Dark, tarry stools are a classic warning sign of bleeding in the stomach or intestines. Spotting this early saves lives! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h7)

question: What grooming tip should a nurse give to a patient on long-term blood thinners?

options.A: Use an electric razor instead of a blade
options.B: Stop all dental hygiene care to protect gums
options.C: Avoid brushing teeth to prevent minor bleeding
options.D: Shave with a traditional straight razor daily

explanation: Electric razors are much safer because they prevent accidental nicks and cuts that bleed easily on blood thinners. Smart advice! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h8)

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who forgets to take their daily anticoagulant dose?

options.A: Stop taking the medication for the rest of the week
options.B: Double the next two doses to make up for lost time
options.C: Follow the specific clinic guidelines for missed doses
options.D: Take a double dose immediately to catch up

explanation: Never let a patient guess! Doubling up can cause dangerous bleeding, so they should always check their clinic's missed-dose policy. You nailed it! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h8)
